title: Flat-proper refinement of a finitely presented subtrusive scheme map
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact). The constructible topology of a scheme is locally generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements; A map $a:X\to Y$ is universally subtrusive if, after every affine scheme base change $T\to Y$, it is surjective and quotient in the constructible topology and each specialization pair $t_0\in\overline{\{t_1\}}$ lifts to a specialization pair in $X\times_YT$. Assume $f$ is universally subtrusive. There exist schemes $X_1,Y_1$, maps $u:X_1\to X$, $a:X_1\to Y_1$, and $b:Y_1\to Y$ such that $fu=ba$, $a$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation, and $b$ is proper, surjective and of finite presentation. Faithfully flat means flat and surjective [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]; proper means separated, finite type, and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. In particular $ba$ is a surjective refinement of $f$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ and no flatness hypothesis on $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem (3.10), affine-base case, printed p.14. Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose $p:C\to Y$ from [lem-sfb-affine-integral-compact-generics-cover]. Put $Z=X\times_Y C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $h:Z\to C$ is finitely presented and $Z$ is qcqs. By [lem-sfb-subtrusive-topological-descent-calculus], $h$ is universally subtrusive. All schemes here are quasi-separated, as required by that calculus: $C$ and $Y$ are affine and the maps to them are finitely presented.

source.place: Theorem (3.10), affine case: integral covering with compact generic points

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-compact-generics-flat-open] to $h$: the cover provides reducedness and quasi-compactness of $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$. Obtain a dense quasi-compact open $U\subseteq C$ containing every generic point of an irreducible component of $C$, over which $h$ is flat. Its restriction is locally of finite presentation by base change in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Apply [lem-trf-flattening-by-admissible-blowup] to $Z\to C$ and $U$. Finite presentation gives the required finite type and quasi-separatedness. This gives a $U$-admissible blowup $q:B\to C$ and a closed strict transform $W\subseteq Z\times_C B$ such that $a:W\to B$ is flat and of finite presentation.

source.place: Lemma (3.5) and Proposition (3.6); flattening input is Stacks Tag 081R (flat.tex, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up)

proof.text: The centre ideal is finite type and equal to the unit ideal on $U$ by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Thus [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper] makes $q$ proper, and [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies its inverse image of $U$ with $U$. Its closed image contains dense $U$, so $q$ is surjective. By [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup], the same $U$ is dense in $B$. We have only asserted that $q$ is proper, not that it is finitely presented.

source.place: Proposition (3.6), blowup and dense-open properties; Stacks divisors.tex, blowup geometry

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be the centre of $q$ and $E=V(\mathcal I\mathcal O_B)=q^{-1}(V(\mathcal I))$; since $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, $U\subseteq C\setminus V(\mathcal I)$. Every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $B$ lies in $q^{-1}(U)$: by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], near $\xi$ the ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_B$ is generated by a non-zero-divisor $t$, which stays a non-zero-divisor in the localization $\mathcal O_{B,\xi}$; that local ring has a single prime, so a non-unit $t$ would be nilpotent, impossible; hence $t$ is a unit and $\xi\notin E$. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $B\setminus E\to C\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ is an isomorphism of open subschemes, so $q(\xi)$ is a generic point of an irreducible component of the open $C\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, hence of $C$, and $q(\xi)\in U$ by step 2. (Topological density of $U$ in $B$ alone would not give this when $B$ has infinitely many components.) Now let $b\in B$, choose a generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component containing $b$, and an affine open $T\subseteq B$ containing $b$, hence $\xi$. The base change of $f$ along the affine $T\to Y$ is $(Z\times_CB)\times_BT\to T$, so by the definition of universal subtrusiveness in the statement (equivalently by base change in [lem-sfb-subtrusive-topological-descent-calculus]) the pair $b\in\overline{\{\xi\}}$ lifts to $z\in\overline{\{z_\xi\}}$ in $Z\times_CB$. The strict transform $W$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of the open subscheme of $Z\times_CB$ over $B\setminus E$; the immersion of that open factors through its scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], so $W$ is closed and contains the inverse image of $q^{-1}(U)$. Hence $z_\xi\in W$ and its specialization $z\in W$. Thus $a:W\to B$ is surjective. This is the specialization argument of Rydh Lemma (3.2); it does not assume flatness of $h$.

source.place: Lemma (3.2) and Remark (3.4): write out the specialization lifting, without creating an elementary lemma node

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-in-proper-fp] to $B\to C$: $C$ is affine, hence qcqs, and step 3 proved properness. Write $B=\varprojlim_j B_j$ with $B_j\to C$ proper and finitely presented, and all transitions and projections closed immersions. In particular the transitions are affine. Every $B_j\to C$ is surjective, since the surjective $B\to C$ factors through it. All $B_j$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. This approximation supplies finite presentation without assuming it for the original blowup.

source.place: Tag 09ZR, lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation; agent variant of the finite-presentation preparation in Rydh (3.7)

proof.text: Over the affine-transition system $(B_j)$, apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](1) to the finitely presented $W\to B$. Obtain $W_j\to B_j$ finitely presented. The schemes $Z\times_C B_j$ are also finitely presented over $B_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) to descend the map $W\to Z\times_C B$ to $v_j:W_j\to Z\times_C B_j$ after increasing $j$. This retains the actual map to $X$ as part of the diagram, not merely the abstract existence of a flat scheme.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, (1),(2), over the proper approximating schemes

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] to $W_j\to B_j$, viewed over the system $(B_j)$ with target the identity scheme $B_j$. Their limit map is $a$, flat by step 2 and surjective by step 4; the stage map is finitely presented, and both source and target are qcqs. Choose a common later index where both properties hold. Flatness and surjectivity persist under the intervening base changes by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Thus we have $W_j\to B_j\to C$ with the first arrow faithfully flat and finitely presented and the second proper, surjective and finitely presented.

Fix that index and write $V=W_j$, $D=B_j$. The composite $V\to C$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]; it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since $V,D,C$ are qcqs. Thus $V\to C$ and $D\to C$ are finitely presented. The descended $v_j$ gives a $C$-map $V\to X\times_Y C$ compatible with $V\to D\to C$.

source.place: Composition of local finite presentation (Tag 01TR) and qcqs permanence

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite], write $C=\varprojlim_i C_i$ over $Y$, with $C_i\to Y$ finite and finitely presented and affine transitions. Each $C_i$ is affine and qcqs, and $C_i\to Y$ is surjective because $C\to Y$ factors through it. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the finitely presented $C$-schemes $V,D,X\times_Y C$ and the maps $V\to D$, $V\to X\times_Y C$. Directedness gives a common stage; clause (3) ensures all diagram equalities after increasing it. We obtain finitely presented $V_i,D_i$ over $C_i$ and maps $a_i:V_i\to D_i$, $u_i:V_i\to X$ with $fu_i=(C_i\to Y)(D_i\to C_i)a_i$.

source.place: Tags 09YZ (lemma-integral-limit-finite-and-finite-presentation) and 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation); Rydh Theorem (3.10), final limit argument

proof.text: The map $a_i$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], since $V_i\to C_i$ is locally of finite presentation and $D_i\to C_i$ is locally of finite type. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since $V_i,D_i$ are qcqs, so is finitely presented. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] to $a_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] to $a_i$ and to $D_i\to C_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper] to $D_i\to C_i$. Their limit maps have precisely the needed flatness, surjectivity and properness by step 7. Each stage arrow is locally of finite presentation (hence locally of finite type for properness descent). All schemes are qcqs. Increase $i$ to a common stage; flatness, surjectivity and properness persist under the further base changes by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change].

source.place: Tags 04AI, 07RR, 081F (lemma-eventually-proper); local finite presentation of a map over the base is Tag 02FV

proof.text: Set $X_1=V_i$, $Y_1=D_i$, $u=u_i$, $a=a_i$, and $b=(C_i\to Y)\circ(D_i\to C_i)$. The finite map $C_i\to Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so $b$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Its local finite presentation follows from [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], and its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness from [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; hence $b$ is finitely presented. Both factors of $b$ are surjective, so $b$ is surjective. Step 10 gives the faithfully flat finitely presented $a$, and step 9 gives $fu=ba$. For every $y\in Y$, first choose $y_1$ over $y$ and then $x_1$ over $y_1$; hence $ba$ is a surjective refinement. If $Y$ is empty, take $X_1=Y_1=\varnothing$ and the same conclusions hold vacuously.

source.place: Theorem (3.10), final composition with a finite finitely presented stage
